{{Short description|French astrophysicist (born 1958)}}
{{Rough translation|1=French|date=August 2023}}
[[File:Francois Hammer.png|thumb|François Hammer]]
'''François Hammer''',<ref>{{Cite web|title=François Hammer - Who's Who|url=https://www.whoswho.fr/bio/francois-hammer_73372|access-date=2022-11-12|website=www.whoswho.fr|language=fr}}</ref> born on 19 November 1958, is a French [[astrophysicist]]. He has been an [[astronomer]] at the [[Paris Observatory]] since 1987 and was an astronomer attached to the [[Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope]] between 1991 and 1992.

He has made several discoveries in the fields of [[gravitational lens]]ing, [[cosmology]] and [[Galaxy formation and evolution|galaxy formation]] and structure. He was responsible for the Giraffe [[spectrograph]]<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-11-12|title=ESO - The GIRAFFE Spectrograph|url=https://www.eso.org/sci/facilities/paranal/instruments/flames/inst/Giraffe.html|website=www.eso.org}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> implemented in 2002 at the [[Very Large Telescope]] (VLT). Together with the astronomers Lex Kaper, Per Kjaergaard, Roberto Pallavicini, he was the investigator of the X-shooter<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-11-12|language=en|author1=information@eso.org|title=Most Efficient Spectrograph to Shoot the Southern Skies|url=https://www.eso.org/public/news/eso0920/|website=www.eso.org}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> spectrograph, implemented in 2009 at the VLT.

== Career ==
François Hammer studied at the [[École Centrale des Arts et Manufactures|École centrale des arts et manufactures]] (1980–82), and obtained his [[PhD]] in astrophysics in 1986 at the [[Paris Diderot University|Université Paris-Diderot]]. He was the founding director of the laboratory "Galaxies, Etoiles Physique et Instrumentation" (GEPI, 2002-2009<ref>{{cite journal|language=fr|author1=CNRS|title=Bulletin officiel|journal=Périodique|date=April 2009|url=https://www.dgdr.cnrs.fr/bo/2009/04-09/BO_04_2009.fm.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-11-12|title=Délégations de signature BO 12-2002|url=https://www.dgdr.cnrs.fr/bo/Delegationsdesignature/delsig-bo1202.htm|website=www.dgdr.cnrs.fr}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>). He was elected<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-11-13|title=Note n° 100001ELEC du 9 juillet 2010|url=https://www.dgdr.cnrs.fr/bo/2010/08-09-10/comi-bo080910-not100001elec.htm|website=www.dgdr.cnrs.fr}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> at the Scientific Council of the "Institut national des sciences de l'Univers" du centre national de recherches scientifiques ([[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]]), first secretary (2011–2013) then president<ref>{{cite journal|language=fr|author1=Conseil scientifique de l'INSU|title=Recommandations|journal=Périodique|date=October 2014|url=https://www.cnrs.fr/comitenational/doc/rapport/2014/CS_INSU_Bilan_%20activites_et_%20Recommandations_octobre%202014.pdf}}</ref> in 2014. As a member of the coordination of the National Committee for Scientific Research (2012–2014), he supported the fundamental research for "Assises de l'Enseignement Supérieur et de la Recherche"<ref>{{cite journal|language=fr|author1=Direction du CNRS et Représentation du Comité National de la Recherche Scientifique|title=Une nouvelle ambition pour la recherche|journal=Contribution|date=2012-11-17|url=https://www.cnrs.fr/comitenational/struc_coord/c3n/motions/Assises%20Ambition%20pour%20la%20recherche%20CNRS%20C3N.pdf}}</ref> as well as the employment of scientists.<ref>{{cite journal|language=fr|author1=Représentation du Comité de la Recherche Scientifique (C3N)|title=La crise de l'emploi scientifique en France et ses dangers : introduction à l'analyse chiffrée du Conseil Scientifique du CNRS.|journal=Texte adopté à l'unanimité|date=2014-03-10|url=https://www.cnrs.fr/comitenational/doc/recommandations/2014/C3N_texte_emploi_scientifique_CS_CNRS_mars_2014_version_CS_et_C3N.pdf}}</ref>

He has been partly credited with advancing Franco-Chinese scientific relations in [[astronomy]] and astrophysics through his membership of a Franco-Chinese team at the [[Paris Observatory]].<ref>{{cite press release|date=October 2012 |title=A straightforward tidal mechanism replaces dark matter in dwarfs surrounding the Milky Way|url=https://observatoiredeparis.psl.eu/IMG/pdf/cp_darkmattervo.pdf|location=Paris |publisher=l'Observatoire de Paris |agency=PSL|access-date=2026-01-16}}</ref>

== Research ==
Hammer established the first gravitational lensing model to explain the giant luminous arcs recently{{When|date=August 2023}} discovered in [[Galaxy cluster|galaxy clusters]].<ref>{{cite book|author1=Jim Peebles|date=2020-06-02|language=en|location=Princeton|page=244|publisher=Princeton University Press|title=Cosmology's Century: An Inside History of Our Modern Understanding of the Universe}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite journal|language=en|author1=Francois Hammer|title=A gravitational lensing model of the strange ring-like structure in A370.|journal=Proceeding of the Third IAP Workshop|date=1987-01-01|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1987hrpg.work..467H|access-date=2022-11-12|pages=467–473|bibcode=1987hrpg.work..467H }}</ref> This had led to a new estimate of galaxy cluster masses.

Very few distant galaxies were known in the 80s; together with the astronomers David Crampton, [[Olivier Le Fèvre]] and Simon Lilly, Hammer carried out the first spectroscopic survey of a thousand galaxies up to z=1 (Canada-France Redshift Survey). From this, the team discovered that star formation in the Universe had decreased by a factor of ten over the last 8 billion years, a result confirmed using [[infrared]] data to account for the dust-enshrouded star formation.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=S. J. Lilly|author2=O. Le Fevre|author3=F. Hammer|author4=David Crampton|title=The Canada-France Redshift Survey: The Luminosity Density and Star Formation History of the Universe to Z approximately 1|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=460|date=1996-03-01|issn=0004-637X|doi=10.1086/309975|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1996ApJ...460L...1L|access-date=2022-11-12|pages=L1|arxiv=astro-ph/9601050 |bibcode=1996ApJ...460L...1L |s2cid=18098246 }}</ref>

He implemented the first 3D multi-spectroscopy system on an 8- meter class telescope,<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-11-12|language=en|author1=information@eso.org|title=Multiple Eyes for the VLT - First System of Deployable Multi-Integral Field Units Ready|url=https://www.eso.org/public/news/eso0203/|website=www.eso.org}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and invented the new concept of 'morpho-kinematics'<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-11-12|language=en|author1=information@eso.org|title=Hubble and ESO's VLT provide unique 3D views of remote galaxies|url=https://www.spacetelescope.org/announcements/ann0903/|website=www.spacetelescope.org}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> to identify the physical processes that govern galaxy formation, by combining the deep morphologies of HST with the 3D spectroscopy performed at the VLT.<ref name=":02">{{cite book|author1=François Hammer, Mathieu Puech, Hector Flores, Myriam Rodrigues|date=November 2016|isbn=9781786340566|language=en|publisher=World Scientific|title=Studying Distant Galaxies: A Handbook Of Methods And Analyses}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

Together with colleagues and his students, he discovered that the morphologies of present-day galaxies can be explained by major mergers of gas-rich galaxies, after which the gas is gradually wrapped around the center to form a new disk. This new concept of post-merger disk formation<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-11-12|title=ESA Science & Technology - The evolution of the Hubble sequence|url=https://sci.esa.int/web/hubble/-/46421-the-evolution-of-the-hubble-sequence|website=sci.esa.int}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=F. Hammer|author2=H. Flores|author3=M. Puech|author4=Y. B. Yang|title=The Hubble sequence: just a vestige of merger events?|journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics|volume=507|date=2009-12-01|issue=3 |issn=0004-6361|doi=10.1051/0004-6361/200912115|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009A&A...507.1313H|access-date=2022-11-12|pages=1313–1326|arxiv=0903.3962 |bibcode=2009A&A...507.1313H |s2cid=9355758 }}</ref> indicates that the hierarchical scenario applies to all galaxy types, either spiral or elliptical. Furthermore, this disk rebuilding scenario solves the so-called spin catastrophe by providing large angular momentum to spiral galaxies. In 2007, he showed that the [[Milky Way]] is quite exceptional, as it has not been affected by a collision since the earliest epochs.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=F. Hammer|author2=M. Puech|author3=L. Chemin|author4=H. Flores|title=The Milky Way, an Exceptionally Quiet Galaxy: Implications for the Formation of Spiral Galaxies|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=662|date=2007-06-01|issue=1 |issn=0004-637X|doi=10.1086/516727|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007ApJ...662..322H|access-date=2022-11-12|pages=322–334|arxiv=astro-ph/0702585 |bibcode=2007ApJ...662..322H |s2cid=18002823 }}</ref> This was confirmed in 2018 by [[Gaia (spacecraft)|Gaia]] observations that have identified the remains of a large collision called [[Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus]] which took place nearly 10 billion years ago.<ref>{{cite journal|language=en|author1=Vasily Belokurov|title=Co-formation of the disc and the stellar halo|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|date=2018|volume=478 |issue=1 |page=611 |doi=10.1093/mnras/sty982 |doi-access=free |arxiv=1802.03414 |bibcode=2018MNRAS.478..611B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|language=en|author1=Misha Haywood|title=In Disguise or Out of Reach: First Clues about In Situ and Accreted Stars in the Stellar Halo of the Milky Way from Gaia DR2|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|date=2018|volume=863 |issue=2 |page=113 |doi=10.3847/1538-4357/aad235 |arxiv=1805.02617 |bibcode=2018ApJ...863..113H |s2cid=119392868 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

He produced the most accurate modeling of the large [[Andromeda Galaxy|Andromeda galaxy]] with his colleagues, Yanbin Yang and Jianling Wang. This has shown that Andromeda was the result of a major collision two to three billion years ago,<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-11-12|date=2018-02-21|language=fr|title=La nouvelle histoire de la galaxie d'Andromède|url=https://www.radiofrance.fr/franceinter/podcasts/la-une-de-la-science/la-nouvelle-histoire-de-la-galaxie-d-andromede-5023619|website=France Inter}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=F. Hammer|author2=Y. B. Yang|author3=J. L. Wang|author4=R. Ibata|title=A 2-3 billion year old major merger paradigm for the Andromeda galaxy and its outskirts|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|volume=475|date=2018-02-01|issue=2 |issn=0035-8711|doi=10.1093/mnras/stx3343|pages=2754–2767|doi-access=free |arxiv=1801.04279 |bibcode=2018MNRAS.475.2754H }}</ref> explaining the overall properties of the galaxy. He also modeled the large [[Magellanic Stream]] of neutral hydrogen,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=F. Hammer|author2=Y. B. Yang|author3=J. L. Wang|author4=R. Ibata|title=A 2-3 billion year old major merger paradigm for the Andromeda galaxy and its outskirts|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|volume=475|date=2018-02-01|issue=2 |issn=0035-8711|doi=10.1093/mnras/stx3343|pages=2754–2767|doi-access=free |arxiv=1801.04279 |bibcode=2018MNRAS.475.2754H }}</ref> still unexplained since its discovery, 40 years ago.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Don Mathewson|title=Discovery of the Magellanic Stream|journal=Journal of Astronomical History and Heritage|volume=15|date=2012-07-01|issue=2 |issn=1440-2807|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012JAHH...15..100M|access-date=2022-11-12|pages=100–104|doi=10.3724/SP.J.1440-2807.2012.02.03 |bibcode=2012JAHH...15..100M |s2cid=220743599 }}</ref> He is currently{{When|date=December 2023}} researching the origin of [[Dwarf galaxy|dwarf galaxies]] near the Milky Way, using astrometric data from the Gaia satellite.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-11-12|language=en|title=Gaia reveals that most Milky Way companion galaxies are newcomers to our corner of space|url=https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Gaia/Gaia_reveals_that_most_Milky_Way_companion_galaxies_are_newcomers_to_our_corner_of_space|website=www.esa.int}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Prizes ==
* Médaille de bronze du CNRS, 1987
* [[Descartes-Huygens Prize]] given by the [[French Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]], 2011<ref>{{Cite journal|author1=Académie des Sciences et Académie Royale des lettres et des sciences des Pays-Bas|date=March 2012|title=Le prix Descartes-Huygens 2012|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/presse/communique/prixdescartes_190312.pdf|journal=Communiqué de presse|language=fr}}</ref>
